How can molecular, physiological and population evidence improve diagnosis and treatment of disease?
How do biological systems produce brain function, behaviour and cognition?

alternatives.label: Biology across organisms, ecosystems & health
alternatives.concept: Study living systems from biodiversity, evolution and ecosystems to cells, biochemistry, human physiology, genetics and disease. Laboratory work, statistics and data analysis support these biological questions; environmental science, sustainability governance and ethics add complementary perspectives.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum gives substantial weight to organismal and ecological biology and to human health and molecular biology, so the label describes its broad biological span rather than presenting one subfield as dominant.

alternatives.label: Ecology, climate & environmental biology
alternatives.concept: Study biodiversity, evolution, ecosystems and conservation alongside climate change and environmental systems. Spatial analysis, soils, biogeochemistry and sustainability research connect ecological questions with environmental assessment; governance, justice and resource geoscience provide complementary approaches.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by ecology, biodiversity, environmental science, climate, conservation and sustainability, with methods and governance supporting that biological focus.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces twelve courses in molecular, biomedical, physiological and disease study with climate, conservation, environmental systems, spatial observation, soils, adaptation, sustainable farming and environmental-justice study.

alternatives.label: Human biology, neuroscience & health psychology
alternatives.concept: Study molecular and cellular biology, human physiology, infection, genetics and disease together with neurobiology and cognition. A substantial psychology strand examines behaviour, mental health, development and assessment. Laboratory work, epidemiology, statistics and research synthesis support this combination; it is not a specialist medical or clinical qualification. Normative ethical reasoning complements the biological and psychological inquiry; this is not professional clinical-psychology training.
alternatives.labelReason: Human/molecular/physiological/neurobiological core plushealth/behaviouralmethods andethicalreasoning; clinicalpsychodiagnostic/therapycourse removed asweakerbiologicalcontribution.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces ten ecology, evolution, sustainability, conservation and environmental courses with a sequenced brain-and-behaviour, cognition, health psychology, development, diagnosis and research strand; it differs from the environmental route by twenty-two courses.

candidates.label: Microbiology, functional genomics and physiological adaptation

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Biology bachelor. The official curriculum offers seven subject-specific domain specialisations and an eighth Free domain explicitly intended for students who cannot or do not want to select one domain. The Free domain is therefore the least specialised official continuation of the broad first-year foundation and is selected independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest response sustains direct biological inquiry through ecology/evolution and molecular/cellular/human biology, not merely neighbouring science. The second direction changes the focus to ecology, climate and environmental assessment; the third combines human biology and neuroscience with a substantial psychological approach to health and behaviour. Their twelve, ten and twenty-two course differences have substantive purposes. Three alternatives have been implemented. The remaining microbiology/genomics/physiological-adaptation candidate contains valid target interests, but no fourth programme or validated specialist implementation is claimed. blocks: Both develop evolutionary explanations of adaptation and organismal diversity; UCR covers evolution across taxa rather than concentrating on animal anatomy.
Both introduce biological diversity across organisms and ecological settings.
Both examine ecosystem function and interactions between organisms and their environment.

Both examine biochemical reactions and molecular mechanisms in living systems.
Both examine molecular and cellular processes, regulation and biological information.
Both examine inheritance and genetic mechanisms; UCR concentrates on molecular pathology and genetics.

Both directly study human organ systems and physiology. UCR Human Physiology covers homeostasis, organ-system function and integration; its narrower physiological focus does not reproduce all of the external Human Biology component.

Partial substantive microbiology relationship through aseptic culture, bacterial identification, sterilisation, antibiotic testing and transformation. The UCR laboratory scope does not cover the full Radboud microbial curriculum.
Direct biological nervous-system and behaviour relationship through comparative anatomy, regulation and biological rhythms; coverage differs.
UCR covers anatomy, physiology and disease but has no dedicated histology course.

Both teach multiple regression and analysis of variance as important statistical methods. Radboud also includes Bayesian testing and diagnostic procedures; UCR additionally covers factor analysis and logistic regression. Partial correspondence, not identical scope or software.

The direct partial overlap is hands-on analysis and visualisation of large datasets, an explicit part of the external programme description. UCR Data Science does not teach genome sequencing, genomic databases or genomic interpretation; the genomic subject remains a substantial difference.
Partial ethical-reasoning relationship through moral theories and argument evaluation. UCR does not establish the whole philosophy-of-science and scientific-integrity component.

Both engage critically with scientific literature and evidence. UCR teaches systematic reviews and meta-analysis, including analysis in R; it is not a dedicated biology essay or a primary-data biological research project.
UCR's scheduled programmes use statistics and data-science methods but do not include a dedicated mathematics-for-biologists course.

Radboud requires a separate introductory course in data organisation, experimental design and univariate hypothesis testing. UCR’s single scheduled statistics course is shown against the closer multifactorial Statistics II component.
Radboud explicitly teaches communicating science to non-specialist readers. General academic writing elsewhere in UCR does not establish this dedicated public-science-writing course.
Radboud requires a 12-EC internship in a research department. UCR's standardized optional independent-research element is shown alongside this component.
Both introduce environmental systems and the scientific assessment of environmental problems.
Both develop reflective academic and professional formation across the bachelor programme.

notes.text: The broad UCR option combines ecological and human/molecular biology. The environmental option devotes more study to climate, Earth systems, resources and governance; the human option includes substantial health psychology. None reproduces Radboud’s dedicated plant physiology and development, broad microbiology and microbial metabolism, histology, extensive domain specialisation or required research-department internship. Optional UCR independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 EC and is not a guaranteed Biology placement.

audience.programmeDescription: Radboud Biology combines organismal, ecological, molecular and medical biology. Students build a broad foundation, develop research skills and choose a domain before completing a research internship.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options emphasise broad biological science, environmental biology, or human biology and neuroscience with health psychology. They differ from Radboud’s plant physiology and development, microbial metabolism, extensive domain study and compulsory research internship. UCR optional independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC and does not guarantee a Biology placement.

curriculum.limitation: The adopted curriculum contains 36 EC of restricted choices and 30 EC of free electives. Choices and the final project require the applicable approval and prior preparation; prospective 2027–2028 overviews may change.

componentNotes.bio3-internship: The individual final project is a 12-EC research internship. Entry requires at least 120 EC including the complete first year, and prior project approval. An extension of up to 3 EC uses elective space and must be agreed in the internship plan.
componentNotes.bio2-domain: 36 EC of restricted choices includes a 30-EC personalised domain from approved BB1/BB2 lists and further restricted electives.
componentNotes.bio3-domain: 30 EC of assessable academic bachelor electives. BB1/BB2 courses and a coherent minor of 15–30 EC are recommended.
componentNotes.bio3-ppd: Personal and Professional Development starts in year 1 and is signed off later. Introductory and research skills are embedded in first-year courses; compulsory RADAr adds no credits. The normal first-year study-advice threshold is 39 of 60 EC, subject to personal circumstances.
